inbrief: Albanese: COP31 failure a sign of 'difficult geopolitical times'.
Guterres: "There may be no consensus in the negotiating room. There is no ambiguity in the science."
The $120bn adaptation finance target was dropped from the final COP31 draft.
China and India accepted the COP31 text; Russia could not accept fossil-fuel wording.
Ed Yardeni cuts his S&P 500 target to 7,500 from 7,900.
Taiwan's shares fell 17% in a week — their worst since 1990.
Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Wadkute dies of cardiac arrest in Delhi.
Tata Steel seals a ₹28,000 crore deal with APL Apollo.
US and Venezuela sign a deal to re-establish military ties.
Bukele seeks a third term as president of El Salvador.
Guatemala decrees a state of emergency after a murder spree claims a lawmaker.
Nine killed as a pilgrims' vehicle rams a truck in Rajasthan's Kota.

lead.body: Wall Street fell for a seventh straight session on Friday as chip stocks plunged 10.6% and the VIX jumped 26% to 35.89. On Monday, Nasdaq 100 futures rebounded nearly 3% and S&P 500 futures rose about 2%, while South Korea's Kospi slid more than 3% at the open and Taiwan's shares — down 17% for the week, their worst since 1990 — faced a short-selling ban. Japan's markets were closed for a holiday; gold rose 1.1% to $3,577 and Brent slipped to $91.78.
lead.deck: US futures bounce as Asia slides and governments step in — Taiwan bans short-selling, China cuts margin rules and South Korea readies stabilisation funds after Friday's wipeout sent the S&P 500 down 3.7% and the Nasdaq 5.3%.
lead.headline: THE AI ROUT GOES GLOBAL

lead2.deck: COP31 ended with no deal — the first climate summit to fail since 2009. The UN chief is "deeply disappointed"; campaigners call it the worst COP ever. The $120bn adaptation target is gone; the next attempt is Addis Ababa in 2027.
lead2.headline: AFTER THE COLLAPSE
